title: Rigid Drawer Box Design: Fit, Insert and Ribbon Pull
seoTitle: Rigid Drawer Box Design: An MTT 24-Truffle Case
summary: An MTT 24-truffle quotation shows what to check in rigid drawer box design: sleeve fit, loaded height, insert clearance and the fabric pull.
intro: For rigid drawer box design, approve the sleeve, loaded tray and pull together. An empty drawer that slides freely can behave differently once the insert and products are fitted. In this MTT quotation for 24 truffles, the 220 × 160 × 30 mm external size was specified, while the usable capacity, drawer clearance and pull detail still required sample approval.
sections: The quoted box: 24 truffles, with the fit still open

Our 7 October 2026 quotation called for an assembled rigid drawer box: an outer sleeve, a sliding tray and a paperboard insert for 24 truffles. The outside measured 220 × 160 × 30 mm on the quotation. The same record left the insert layout, usable capacity and drawer clearance to be checked against the truffles and their liners before production.

That distinction matters. The outside size describes the package the buyer receives. It does not tell the packer how much room remains above a chocolate or beside the insert.

This is an anonymised quotation-stage case. The available record does not establish an approved sample, completed production or measured opening performance. Customer identity and commercial prices are withheld.
Three places a drawer can catch

Start with the sleeve and tray. Check the finished wrapped surfaces, especially the sleeve mouth, corners and paper joins. If the tray catches at one point, find the contact mark before increasing every dimension. A local overlap and a tray that is too large need different corrections.

Next, fit the insert. It should stay seated without pushing the tray walls outward. Then load the contents with the intended liners. Check whether anything rises into the sleeve opening as the drawer moves; a fit check on the empty box misses that contact.

For this 24-truffle brief, we would check the tray first without the insert, then with the insert, and finally with the truffles and liners. Keeping those observations separate helps identify which component needs a revision.
Why we have not supplied a universal clearance

The quotation gives board weight, but not enough information to calculate a finished sliding gap. The wrap, lining, joints and actual board thickness all need to be represented in the sample. Our GSM and thickness case explains why a grammage line cannot be used as a caliper measurement.

Humidity is another reason to record how a sample was checked. RISE describes moisture-driven dimensional changes in paper and paperboard, including curl and waviness.[2] A drawer comparison made under different conditions may therefore need investigation before the drawing is changed.

For its paperboard printing and converting guidance, Holmen recommends 45–60% relative humidity and 20–23°C to help prevent curl and misregistration.[1] Those are the manufacturer’s processing recommendations, not a storage specification for the chocolates, a drawer tolerance or evidence that Holmen board was used in this MTT quote.

Agree the sample conditions with the converter and record them. We would approve an opening range using the final materials and representative loaded samples, rather than promise one gap for every drawer box.
Pull the tray where the customer will pull it

The quote specifies a fabric pull but leaves its detail to sample approval. A decorative ribbon shown in artwork is not enough to settle the attachment.

On the sample, pull from the position a customer can actually reach. Check whether the tray moves straight, whether the attachment lifts the lining and whether loose fabric catches inside the sleeve. Keep the intended contents in place while checking. If the pull bends or tears the front before the drawer moves, first investigate the resistance and attachment together.

Record the attachment detail, visible length and agreed opening checks on the sample sheet. A pull-force measurement or repeated-opening result belongs there only after it has been measured. Neither is available for this quotation.
Keep a short fit record beside the approved sample

CheckRecord before release

DecisionAccepted details, required changes and who confirms the next sample

Food-contact barriers and liners were also left for approval in the quotation. Resolving the drawer fit does not resolve that suitability question. Keep it as a separate approval item for the actual materials and intended use.

The sample approval checklist covers the wider approval record. Transport protection also needs its own review of the complete packed unit and outer carton; smooth drawer travel is not a shipping test.

Case data: MTT quotation dated 7 October 2026, checked against its construction, material, dimensions and fit-approval entries. The quotation supports the specification and outstanding decisions, not a completed project outcome.

[1] Holmen, General Technical Information, issued 10 December 2025, paperboard handling section. [2] RISE, Hygroexpansion of paper and paperboard. Both checked 26 October 2026.

cta: Send the product and liner dimensions, a photo of the packed arrangement, quantity and any existing drawer sample. MTT can review the sleeve, tray, insert and pull as one assembly and identify what the next sample needs to confirm.
